summary: Live bench of myiotsan's active network discovery scan (tools/fleetbench/bench_iotsan_discovery.py, 38 checks) against the four safety claims infra/iot/discover's package doc makes for every scanner it ships: READ-ONLY, LAN-local, bounded, cancellable - plus that a scan proposes candidates and never adds a device, that it is opt-in/admin-only, and that it is audited. A new modbus_tripwire.py stands up a real Modbus TCP device that answers as a plausible SunSpec device and records the function code of every request, splitting reads from writes, and deliberately accepts a write with a success reply (rather than an exception) so a scanner falling back to a read path on failure cannot hide the evidence; a Blackhole socket that accepts and never answers is what actually exercises a per-host timeout, since a closed port fails instantly and proves nothing. The bench found one real defect: LAN-local was stated in the package doc but never enforced. The multicast scanners (mDNS/SSDP/EtherNet-IP/BACnet) are link-local by construction, but the Modbus sweep takes its target from a CIDR string an admin types, and nothing checked it - a running appliance accepted and really ran a sweep of 192.0.2.0/24 (public TEST-NET-1 address space, 6.4s) and of 127.0.0.1/32 (the appliance's own loopback), making the scan endpoint a general-purpose port scanner pointed wherever the appliance has a route. Fixed in discover.Hosts, the one funnel every sweep target passes through: a new checkLANLocal/isLANLocal pair refuses anything outside RFC 1918 + RFC 6598 CGNAT + RFC 3927 IPv4 link-local + IPv6 ULA/link-local, and refuses loopback, unspecified and multicast addresses outright. A bare hostname is resolved and every address it yields must qualify; an unresolvable target is refused rather than scanned (fail closed); a list with one bad target among good ones is refused whole; CIDR bounds are checked before expansion so a wide public range is refused on sight. Five new unit tests in infra/iot/discover/discover_test.go. After the fix the refusal is instant (0.0s) where the sweep used to cost 6.4s, and a genuine LAN range still scans normally. Everything else in the safety posture held and is now proven live rather than merely designed that way: the entire scan against the tripwire issued exactly four requests, all function code 3 (read holding registers), and no write ever arrived; a /8 is refused before any probe goes out; a stalling host is bounded by the per-op timeout; abandoning the request mid-scan stops further dialling; a scan produces candidates and adds no device; operator and viewer are both refused the scan and window endpoints; and a scan is recorded in the notification feed. Also documented as an honest limit, not a defect: the scan is synchronous and holds its HTTP request open for its whole duration (measured up to 41.7s at the full host cap with all five scanners selected), which only completes because myiotsan's shipped config disables the write timeout - noted on ScanService's own doc comment so the host cap and that timeout are never tuned independently. 38/38 with the fix; 36/38 against the unfixed app.
compatibility: Backward-compatible for every legitimate use. No API shape, schema or config default changes. The only behavior change is a new refusal: POST /api/discovery/scan with a Modbus CIDR or bare host outside private/link-local address space (or its own loopback) is now rejected with an explanatory error instead of actually sweeping; any range a site genuinely numbers its equipment out of (RFC 1918, RFC 6598 CGNAT, RFC 3927 link-local, IPv6 ULA/link-local) is unaffected and continues to scan exactly as before. A device outside those ranges can still be added by hand, deliberately, through the existing manual-provisioning path - this only constrains automatic discovery. Existing installs need no migration or config change; the mDNS/SSDP/EtherNet-IP/BACnet scanners are untouched (they were already link-local by construction).
